newsitem.title: USA: International Paper posts loss after Scitex charge.
newsitem.headline: International Paper posts loss after Scitex charge.

text.p: International Paper Co. Tuesday reported a fourth-quarter loss after writing down its investment in Scitex, a troubled Israeli high-technology company.
IP lost $5 million, or 2 cents a share, in the quarter ended Dec. 31, versus profits of $263 million, or $1.01 a share, in the year-ago period. Sales were flat at $5.1 billion.
The results include a pre-tax charge of $165 million, or $105 million after taxes, for the write-down, as well as IP's share of a restructuring charge announced by Scitex in November.

IP, together with Discount Investment Corp., Clal Electronics and PEC Israel Economic Corp., own 36 percent of Scitex, which manufactures digital equipment for the printing, video and graphic arts industries.

Once the flagship of Israel's high-tech sector, Scitex reported a $151 million loss in the third quarter, largely due to write-downs and restructuring costs in its graphic arts division. Its stock has plunged from $44 in 1992 to $10.75 Tuesday, down 12.5 cents on the day on Nasdaq.
"As we begin a new year, marketplace fundamentals are improving," said International Paper's Chairman and Chief Executive John Dillon.

"Volumes are good, and inventories are declining. Although traditional seasonal weakness and the impact of current low prices are likely to continue to affect earnings in the short-term, we expect prices for many of our products to recover early in the year."

IP said fourth-quarter earnings from printing papers fell from the prior quarter due to weaker prices, lower uncoated papers volume and start-up costs to convert a paper machine to a new product line at the company's mill in Jay, Maine.

Earnings from the company's packaging businesses fell mainly because of downtime to control inventory at containerboard mills and higher costs for such items as energy, IP said. Demand for packaging grades, particularly containerboard exports, was strong during the quarter, while prices for bleached folding carton grades rose late in the quarter.
Speciality products' earnings slid from the third quarter, mainly due to seasonal weakness. But this was partially offset by the petroleum business, which benefited from higher prices.
Earnings from forest products fell from the prior quarter because of lower harvest volumes and weak panel markets in the United States.
IP also said it is benefiting from its $3.5 billion merger with Federal Paper Board, which was completed in March.

"We are achieving, ahead of schedule, our target of reducing costs by $100 million, on an annualized basis, as a result of our merger," Dillon said. "And we expect additional savings this year to result from the excellent assets and outstanding customer focus represented by the former Federal Paper Board businesses."
IP, based in Purchase, N.Y., has 27 U.S. mills and operations in 31 countries, with 88,000 employees worldwide.
IP's stock was unchanged at $42.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
